title: NCCIA cybercrime complaint portal
summary: Pakistan's NCCIA provides an official online complaint registration channel for cybercrime cases.

sections.title: Preserve evidence
sections.text: Before reporting, keep copies of suspicious messages, screenshots, sender identifiers, URLs, dates, transaction references, and other evidence. Avoid deleting the original evidence until copies are preserved.

sections.title: Submit an official complaint
sections.text: Use the official NCCIA complaint portal for cybercrime complaints in Pakistan. Provide accurate incident details and supporting evidence. ScamShield should never claim that submitting a complaint guarantees investigation or recovery.

sections.title: Financial-loss response
sections.text: When money was transferred, contact the bank, card issuer, wallet, or payment provider immediately in addition to preserving evidence and reporting the cybercrime.

title: National CERT guidance on phishing
summary: National CERT Pakistan publishes public guidance for recognizing and reducing phishing risk.

sections.title: Phishing warning signs
sections.text: Treat unexpected requests for credentials, financial information, attachments, or urgent account action as suspicious. Branding and familiar names do not prove authenticity.

sections.title: Verify independently
sections.text: Do not use contact details or links supplied in a suspicious message. Verify the organization through an independently known official website, app, phone number, or other trusted channel.

sections.title: Protect accounts
sections.text: Use strong unique passwords and multi-factor authentication. If credentials may have been exposed, change them from a trusted device and review account sessions.

title: WhatsApp Account Hijacking Campaign advisory
summary: A 2026 National CERT advisory describes social-engineering paths used to hijack WhatsApp accounts, including verification-code theft, call forwarding, phishing, and QR-code manipulation.

sections.title: Verification-code theft
sections.text: Attackers may impersonate a trusted contact, support staff, or service provider and ask for a WhatsApp verification code. Do not share the code with another person.

sections.title: QR-code and linked-device abuse
sections.text: Treat unexpected QR-code scanning instructions as high risk because they may link an attacker's device or enable unauthorized access.

sections.title: Account recovery
sections.text: If takeover is suspected, use WhatsApp's official recovery and security controls, review linked devices, strengthen account protection, and warn trusted contacts about possible impersonation.

title: Secure online transaction guidance
summary: National CERT Pakistan maintains public guidance for safer online transactions.

sections.title: Before paying
sections.text: Pause when a sender creates urgency. Verify the merchant or recipient independently, check the exact destination, and do not disclose OTPs, PINs, passwords, or recovery codes.

sections.title: After a suspicious payment
sections.text: Preserve the payment record and contact the relevant financial institution or payment service promptly. Ask about available fraud or reversal procedures without assuming recovery is guaranteed.

title: Combatting job scams
summary: National CERT Pakistan includes job-scam awareness in its public cyber-safety program.

sections.title: Job-scam red flags
sections.text: Unexpected recruiter messages, unrealistic pay, vague duties, pressure to move to messaging apps, requests for fees, or requests for sensitive identity information should be treated cautiously.

sections.title: Verify the employer
sections.text: Check the employer through its independently located official website and published contact channels. Do not rely only on logos, screenshots, or contact details sent by the recruiter.

title: What to do if you were scammed
summary: FTC consumer guidance explains immediate recovery actions after payments, credential disclosure, or device access in scam incidents.

sections.title: If you paid
sections.text: Contact the bank, card issuer, payment app, transfer service, or other payment provider promptly, report the fraudulent transaction, and ask whether it can be stopped, reversed, or refunded.

sections.title: If you shared account credentials
sections.text: Change exposed passwords from a trusted device, change reused passwords elsewhere, enable two-factor authentication, and review account access.

sections.title: If someone accessed your device
sections.text: Update security software, scan the device, remove identified threats, change passwords, enable stronger authentication, and review financial or online accounts for unauthorized activity.

title: Job scams
summary: FTC guidance highlights common job-scam patterns, especially payment demands, fake checks, and unrealistic earnings.

sections.title: Pay-to-work warning
sections.text: A job offer that requires payment to obtain the job, training, certification, equipment, or access is a strong warning sign. Verify employers independently before sharing personal information.

sections.title: Fake-check pattern
sections.text: Be cautious when an employer sends a check and instructs you to send part of the money elsewhere or buy gift cards. A check can appear available before it is later identified as fraudulent.

title: Investment scams
summary: FTC guidance warns that investment scams commonly promise large or easy returns with little risk and may start through social media or messaging.

sections.title: Unrealistic promises
sections.text: Promises of guaranteed profit, unusually high returns, little or no risk, secret systems, or pressure to act quickly are major investment-scam indicators.

sections.title: Independent research
sections.text: Research the company, person, platform, and investment independently. Do not rely on testimonials, screenshots of profits, or dashboards supplied by the promoter.

title: Romance scams
summary: FTC consumer guidance describes romance scammers who build trust online and later request money or introduce fraudulent investment opportunities.

sections.title: Relationship-to-money pattern
sections.text: A person met online may quickly move communication off-platform, claim to be far away, build emotional trust, and later ask for money for emergencies, travel, or investment.

sections.title: Protect yourself
sections.text: Slow the interaction down, discuss the situation with someone you trust, independently verify claims, and do not send money or cryptocurrency to someone you have only met online.
